A patch release completing the Javadoc repair that 0.2.1 started. If you are on
0.2.1 the code is identical — upgrade only for complete API documentation.

## What was still wrong

0.2.0 published an empty Javadoc jar. 0.2.1 fixed that, but not completely: its
jar has every page except one, and 32 `{@link}` references across the message,
hook and permission types pointed at that missing page and resolved to nothing —
dead text where a link belonged, and 32 warnings on every build.

The missing page is `in.vidyalai.claude.sdk.types`, and the cause is the same
`Automatic-Module-Name` that emptied 0.2.0's jar. Adding it makes
`maven-javadoc-plugin` treat the project as a named module and switch to modular
processing, which this SDK has no `module-info.java` to satisfy. 0.2.1 contained
that with `legacyMode=true`, which does hold the plugin on non-modular
processing — but also silently drops any package containing nothing but a
`package-info.java`, and `in.vidyalai.claude.sdk.types` is exactly that.

Measured across all three configurations:

| Configuration | javadoc jar | `types` page | warnings |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Automatic-Module-Name`, no `legacyMode` | 532 B | no | — (0.2.0) |
| `Automatic-Module-Name` + `legacyMode` | 1,358,002 B | no | 32 (0.2.1) |
| **neither** | **1,366,232 B** | **yes** | **0** |

`Automatic-Module-Name` arrived in 0.2.0 as a no-cost convenience for JPMS
consumers, and has since cost two Javadoc regressions. It is removed. The honest
way to get a stable module name is a real `module-info.java`, which this SDK
does not have yet; until then JPMS consumers fall back to the filename-derived
`claude.agent.sdk.java`, exactly as they did through 0.1.25. A comment on
`maven-jar-plugin` records the reasoning so it is not re-added without that
`module-info.java`.

Nothing else changed: same code, same Java 17 baseline, same 1056 tests.
